title: David and Jonathan
hookLine: David mourns Jonathan's love as wonderful

lines: THY LOVE TO ME WAS WONDERFUL.
THE KING'S SON, AND HIS RIVAL.
cards: "Thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women." A warrior sings that over a dead friend. The news has just reached David: King Saul and his son Jonathan have fallen in battle on Mount Gilboa.
Saul has hunted David. Jonathan was Saul's son, the heir to the throne David would one day take. By the usual rules of politics, they should have been rivals.
Instead, near the end of David's lament, come Jonathan's name and that line. Today: how it began, what it cost, and what came after.

teach.b: It begins with a sentence that doesn't sound like politics at all. After David's victory over Goliath, "the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul."

teach.h: A PRINCE GIVES AWAY HIS ROBE.
teach.b: Then Jonathan takes off his own robe and gives it to David, with his sword, his bow and his belt. Some readers see a prince handing over the signs of his rank. Then the friendship gets expensive.

Saul wants David dead, and Jonathan, caught between his father and his friend, warns David at real risk to himself. Later he says it outright: you shall be king over Israel, and I shall be next to you.
The heir steps aside in his own words. Readers have heard this bond in more than one way; the text itself calls it love and a covenant.
Then, after the grief, once David is king, he asks a question nobody needed him to ask: "Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan's sake?"
There is: Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, living quietly far from court.

teach.h: A SEAT AT THE TABLE FOR HIS SON.
teach.b: David gives him back his grandfather's land and seats him at the king's table for good.
Kindness here is that same Hebrew word from yesterday, chesed. The friend is gone. The friendship keeps going, as a seat at the table for his son.

how: Readers of the Hebrew Bible point to David and Jonathan as a picture of loyal friendship, and some keep up old friendships with letters, calls or visits on anniversaries and holidays.

a royal title passed from a king to his son
a binding promise, like Jonathan's with David

games.q: you're David, now king. your friend Jonathan is dead, and so is the king who hunted you. what do you do about Saul's family?
o: leave them alone and forget them.
ask if anyone is left, to show kindness for Jonathan's sake.
keep an eye on them as rivals.
games.why: David asks whether anyone is left of Saul's house, finds Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, returns his land and seats him at his table.

practice: Let an old friend come to mind, someone who once stood next to you, at school, at work, in a hard year, whom life has carried somewhere else.
Remember one specific thing, a joke, a kitchen, a drive, something they did for you, and hold it for a few breaths.
Let the first sentence of a note form in your head, not an apology for the silence, just the memory; if you pray, you can give thanks for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Covenant. The binding promise Jonathan made with David, knit together as friends even though one stood between the other and the throne. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: covenant, a binding promise. Jonathan and David make one because Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

carryVoice: Your line: the friend. A covenant can outlive the one who made it. Tomorrow, a love poem.
